author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Mark Stebbins Community Center has opened on Manchester’s West Side, bringing youth programs, health care and family services together in one building. The Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Manchester and Amoskeag Health are anchor tenants, creating a shared location for services that had previously operated through separate organizations.

The center will offer after-school programming, affordable health care, a food pantry, meeting space, community navigators and referrals to other nonprofit support. Its fundraising campaign collected $20.7 million, exceeding an $18.5 million goal after the Catholic Health Care Foundation of Greater Manchester announced a $1 million pledge. The total includes an endowment intended to support long-term operations and maintenance.

The Manchester Housing and Redevelopment Authority provided roughly three acres through a 75-year lease priced at $10 a year, according to remarks at the opening. Federal Community Project Funding secured through the Department of Housing and Urban Development also supported the project. Named for the late businessman and philanthropist Mark Stebbins, the center reflects his goal of helping West Side children and families through coordinated services. With construction complete, the measure of success now shifts from fundraising to how consistently residents can reach and use those programs.
dek: The $20.7 million center combines youth programs, health care, a food pantry and nonprofit support under one roof.
headline: Mark Stebbins Community Center opens on Manchester’s West Side
